subsystems.name: Light engine
subsystems.role: delivers timed light pulses through closed eyelids to influence circadian timing.

subsystems.name: Audio engine
subsystems.role: plays binaural beats or other audio to accompany sleep or relaxation.

subsystems.name: Control unit
subsystems.role: runs the timing program, manages power and connects to a phone.

subsystems.name: Sensors (optional)
subsystems.role: detect sleep stage so stimulation can be timed to it; many masks omit this and rely on a timer.

subsystems.name: Comfort and fit
subsystems.role: keeps the device dark, comfortable and in place through the night.

subsystems.name: Companion app
subsystems.role: lets the user set schedules, choose programs and review sleep data.

buildSteps.title: Design the light path
buildSteps.detail: Choose LED wavelengths (commonly around 470 nm blue and 630 nm red) and arrange them so light reaches the eyes evenly without bright spots.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the electronics
buildSteps.detail: Solder the LEDs, microcontroller, battery and radio onto a flexible circuit board that can bend with the mask.

buildSteps.title: Make the audio system
buildSteps.detail: Mount small speakers or bone-conduction transducers and tune them for low-volume playback that will not disturb sleep.

buildSteps.title: Build the mask body
buildSteps.detail: Cut foam and fabric, insert the electronics, and stitch the layers so the mask blocks outside light and feels soft against the face.

buildSteps.title: Add sensors if used
buildSteps.detail: Place EEG electrodes or motion sensors where they contact the forehead or temples, and secure the wiring.

buildSteps.title: Write firmware
buildSteps.detail: Implement timed light and sound sequences, binaural beat generation, and — where sensors exist — simple sleep-stage detection to trigger stimulation.

buildSteps.title: Develop the app
buildSteps.detail: Create Bluetooth pairing, scheduling controls and a simple dashboard for sleep data.

buildSteps.title: Test for comfort and safety
buildSteps.detail: Check eye safety, skin irritation, battery life over a full night and whether the mask stays in place during movement.

prerequisites.why: they provide the timed light pulses without generating much heat.
they allow sound to be played inside a thin mask without bulky headphones.
they power a full night of operation in a small, light package.
to time stimulation to REM or deep sleep you must know the stage, which is difficult from a mask alone.

prerequisites.tech: Understanding of light's effect on sleep
prerequisites.why: blue light is known to suppress melatonin, but using timed pulses to enhance specific sleep stages is not firmly established.

pathway.milestone: timer-based masks with fixed light and sound programs
pathway.unlocks: consumer devices that aim to support relaxation and circadian routines.

pathway.milestone: masks with EEG or other sensors that detect sleep stage and deliver closed-loop stimulation
pathway.unlocks: stimulation timed to the user's actual sleep cycles rather than a fixed schedule.

pathway.milestone: controlled clinical trials measuring effects on sleep quality and circadian rhythm
pathway.unlocks: evidence to separate effective features from marketing claims.

pathway.milestone: integration with smart home and other wearables for personalised sleep optimisation
pathway.unlocks: coordinated light, sound and temperature changes across the bedroom.
